objects.name: Customer
objects.description: Someone hungry, ordering from the Plum app or the website.

objects.name: Restaurant
objects.description: The kitchen staff who accept an order and mark it ready.

objects.name: Courier
objects.description: Rides or drives the order from the restaurant to the customer's door.

objects.name: Support agent
objects.description: Answers customers and couriers when something goes wrong.

objects.name: Ordering
objects.description:
Everything a customer touches: browsing menus, building a basket, paying.

The **Order API** is the only way in. It keeps orders in Postgres and announces every new
order on the **Order events** bus, which is how **Delivery** hears about it.

objects.name: Delivery
objects.description:
Finds a courier for each order and follows it to the door.

Dispatch matches and offers. Live tracking keeps the customer's map moving.

objects.name: Notifications
objects.description: Push, SMS and email, from one place, so no other system talks to a messaging provider.

objects.name: Back office
objects.description: Tools for Plum's own staff. Nothing here is visible to customers or couriers.

objects.name: Stripe
objects.description:
Takes card payments and sends refunds. Plum never sees a card number.

[Provider status](https://status.stripe.com)

objects.name: Twilio
objects.description: Sends the SMS messages.

objects.name: Mapbox
objects.description: Maps, address lookup and travel times.

objects.name: Customer app
objects.description:
The app on the customer's phone. Browse, order, pay and watch the courier arrive.

Keeps nothing but the basket and the session.

objects.name: Website
objects.description: The same ordering flow in a browser. Menus are rendered on the server so search engines see them.

objects.name: Kitchen tablet
objects.description: Rings when an order arrives. The kitchen taps **Accept**, then **Ready** when it can be collected.

objects.name: Order API
objects.description:
Every client talks to this, and nothing else talks to the **Orders DB**.

- `GET /menus/:restaurant` reads a menu
- `POST /orders` places an order
- `POST /orders/:id/refund` refunds one

objects.name: Orders DB
objects.description: Orders, baskets and refunds. The source of truth for what a customer owes and was charged.

data.name: orders
data.note: One row per order. A refund adds a row to refunds; the order stays.

columns.name: total
columns.note: Stored in cents because rounding broke the first tax run.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.note: Copied from the menu when the order is placed. Later menu changes leave it alone.

shown.name: orders
shown.note: One row per order. A refund adds a row to refunds; the order stays.

objects.name: Menu cache
objects.description: Menus, kept for five minutes. A restaurant's edit shows up on its own once the entry expires.

data.name: Keys
data.limits: Oldest unused go first at 256 MB
data.note: Entries last five minutes because a shorter time put too much load on Postgres.

shown.name: Keys
shown.limits: Oldest unused go first at 256 MB
shown.note: Entries last five minutes because a shorter time put too much load on Postgres.

objects.name: Order events
objects.description:
One message for every change to an order: `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up`, `delivered`.

Dispatch reads from it, and so does the warehouse.

data.name: order-events
data.note: Keyed by order id, so one order's messages stay in order.

shown.name: order-events
shown.note: Keyed by order id, so one order's messages stay in order.

objects.name: Menu
objects.description: Serves a restaurant's menu from the cache, and from the database when the cache is cold.

objects.name: Basket
objects.description: Holds what the customer picked and asks **Pricing** for the running total.

objects.name: Pricing
objects.description:
Works out the total: items, delivery fee (by distance) and any promotion.

The delivery fee uses the travel distance from Mapbox, rounded up to the next 500 m.

snippets.title: Delivery fee

objects.name: Checkout
objects.description:
Prices the basket, authorises the card and places the order.

Nothing is charged until the restaurant accepts. A rejected order releases the hold.

objects.name: Order status
objects.description: Moves an order through `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up` and `delivered`, and announces each step.

snippets.title: Accepting an order
snippets.text:
UPDATE orders
SET status = 'accepted', updated_at = now()
WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'placed'

objects.name: Refunds
objects.description: Returns money to the card, then marks the order refunded. Support can refund in full or by line.

objects.name: Courier app
objects.description: Offers, navigation and proof of delivery. Sends the courier's position every five seconds while a job is open.

objects.name: Dispatch
objects.description:
Turns each new order into a courier on the way.

It reads `placed` events and offers the job to couriers one at a time, nearest first.

objects.name: Live tracking
objects.description: Passes the courier's position to the customer's map. A position older than a minute is dropped.

objects.name: Fleet DB
objects.description: Couriers, their vehicles, and their last known position.

objects.name: Matcher
objects.description: Ranks the idle couriers near a restaurant by how soon each could be there.

objects.name: ETA
objects.description: Estimates travel time from distance, traffic and the courier's vehicle.

objects.name: Offers
objects.description:
Offers a job to one courier at a time and waits 30 seconds for an answer.

A refusal or a timeout moves on to the next courier.

objects.name: Notifier
objects.description: Picks push, SMS or email for each message and sends it. Never blocks the caller.

objects.name: Message templates
objects.description: The wording of every message, per language.

objects.name: Admin dashboard
objects.description: Restaurants, delivery zones, promotions and the weekly reports.

objects.name: Support console
objects.description: Look up an order, see where the courier is, issue a refund.

objects.name: Data warehouse
objects.description: Every order event, kept for reporting. Nothing reads it except the **Admin dashboard**.

steps.text: Announces that the order is paid and carries on without waiting
Hands the event to Dispatch, which starts looking for a courier
Streams the same event to the warehouse for its own records
steps.ends: Order events → Data warehouse in Back office

steps.text: Captures the amount it held
Gives up after five seconds and tries again
Confirms the charge
Marks the order paid
Declines the card
steps.description:
A declined card is not retried. The hold is released and the app asks the customer
for another card.

steps.text: Asks the customer to try another card

charge.text: Waits 1 s, then 2 s, then 4 s between tries. Plum's client gives up after three.

steps.text: About a third of the pings are lost on the way
steps.description:
On a weak signal the app's position pings never reach **Live tracking**. The app does not
retry them: a newer ping is coming in five seconds.

steps.text: The customer's map moves in jumps
steps.ends: Live tracking → Customer app in Ordering

steps.text: Keeps the last position it got
steps.description:
Nothing was written for the lost pings, so the courier can look parked for ten seconds or more
to anything that reads **Fleet DB**, such as the matcher ranking couriers for the next offer.

steps.text: Hears that an order was placed
Finds idle couriers near the restaurant
Ranks them by how soon each could arrive
steps.description:
The **Matcher** asks **ETA** for a travel time per courier, using distance, traffic and the
vehicle. The quickest one is offered the job first.

steps.text: Sends the offer as a push
Accepts within 30 seconds
Streams its position every 5 seconds
steps.description:
Only while a job is open. A position older than a minute is dropped, so a courier who loses
signal stops moving on the customer's map until a fresh position comes in.

steps.text: The customer watches the courier come
steps.ends: Live tracking → Customer app in Ordering

steps.text: Marks the order delivered
steps.ends: Courier app → Order API in Ordering

steps.text: Offers the job, and the nearest courier doesn't answer within 30 seconds
steps.ends: Offers in Dispatch → Notifier in Notifications

steps.text: Moves on to the next courier on the list
Accepts, and the offers stop
Tells the customer that no courier is free yet
steps.ends: Offers in Dispatch → Notifier in Notifications

steps.text: Searches again in a minute

offer.until: a courier accepts, or the list runs out
offer.text: One courier at a time, nearest first. Each has 30 seconds.

steps.text: Fills a basket and taps Place order
POST /orders with the basket
steps.description:
The app sends an idempotency key with the request, so a double tap or a retry on a bad
connection places a single order.

steps.text: Holds the amount on the card
steps.description:
**Checkout** asks Stripe to authorise the total. Nothing is charged yet: the money moves
once the restaurant accepts, and the hold is released if it refuses.

steps.text: Saves the order as placed
Announces the order
Dispatch starts looking for a courier
The restaurant's tablet rings
steps.description:
The kitchen has two minutes to accept. After that the order is cancelled, the hold is
released and the customer is told.

steps.text: Stripe has refunded the charge
steps.description: The money is already back on the customer's card. From here on, Plum's own records are what can go wrong.

steps.text: Can't mark the order refunded, because Orders DB doesn't answer
steps.ends: Refunds in Order API → Orders DB

steps.text: Leaves the order marked paid, though the money is back
Still sends the customer a refund confirmation
steps.ends: Refunds in Order API → Notifier in Notifications

steps.text: Finds the order in the support console
Asks for a refund, in full or by line
The money goes back to the card
steps.description:
Stripe refunds the original charge. The order is marked refunded only once Stripe has
confirmed, so the database never says money was returned that wasn't.

steps.text: Asks for a confirmation to be sent
The customer gets an SMS

flows.name: Stripe goes down and comes back

steps.text: The hold is slow while Stripe shuts down
The hold times out
steps.description: Checkout waits five seconds for the hold and gets no answer. It does not retry while Stripe is down.

steps.text: Offers pay at the door
steps.ends: Checkout in Order API → Customer app

steps.text: The status page says Stripe is restarting
The next check finds it coming back up
The hold goes through

failures.name: Plum fail scenario
failures.about: Made-up ratings for the demo, not a review of anything real.

severity.high: A customer loses money or the kitchen stops

detection.low: An alert fires within a minute

modes.mode: Stripe doesn't answer within five seconds
modes.effect: The order waits on a hold that may or may not exist.
modes.cause: Stripe is slow, or the network between Plum and Stripe drops.
modes.controls: Three tries with backoff. The idempotency key stops a double hold.
modes.action: Page when more than 1% of holds time out for five minutes.

modes.effect: The order is not placed, and the customer is asked for another card.
modes.cause: The card is short of funds, expired or blocked.
modes.controls: The hold is released and the app asks again.

modes.mode: Stripe refunds the money but the database write fails
modes.effect: The customer has the money back, and Plum still shows the order as paid.
modes.cause: Orders DB is out of reach at the moment the refund is saved.
modes.controls: Support can see the refund in Stripe.
modes.action: Compare refunds with Stripe every night.
modes.description:
The refund and the write are two steps, so one can happen without the other.
The nightly comparison only finds the gap.

modes.effect: No order can be placed or read until it is back.
modes.cause: The primary fails, or a failover takes longer than planned.
modes.controls: A standby takes over within a minute.

modes.mode: A double tap places two orders
modes.effect: The customer is charged twice for one basket.
modes.cause: The app sends the order again when the first reply is slow.
modes.controls: Every order carries an idempotency key, and a second order with the same key is refused.

modes.mode: Serves a menu five minutes late
modes.effect: A customer orders a dish the kitchen has just taken off.
modes.cause: The cache refreshes every five minutes.
modes.controls: The kitchen can refuse an item, and the customer is told.

modes.mode: Mapbox calls fail at dinner rush
modes.effect: Dispatch has no travel times, so couriers are matched on distance alone.
modes.cause: Plum passes Mapbox's rate limit once orders pass 900 a minute.
modes.controls: Dispatch falls back to straight-line distance.
modes.action: Batch the travel-time calls, as the second run tries.

modes.effect: Live tracking shows an old position, or none.

modes.mode: Dispatch reads events slower than they arrive
modes.effect: A courier is matched minutes after the customer paid, and the arrival time shown is wrong.
modes.cause: A burst of orders, such as the dinner rush, outruns the one consumer Dispatch runs.
modes.controls: A lag alert fires at 30 seconds.

modes.mode: The tablet goes offline and nobody accepts within two minutes
modes.effect: The customer waits two minutes and then hears that the order was cancelled.
modes.cause: The tablet loses its Wi-Fi, or its battery runs out.
modes.controls: The order cancels itself and the card hold is released.

modes.effect: The order waits for a courier, and the arrival time shown keeps growing.
modes.cause: The couriers near the restaurant are busy, out of signal or away from their phones.
modes.controls: Each offer moves on to the next courier. When the list runs out, the customer is told.
modes.action: Widen the search when the list runs out.

modes.mode: The courier loses signal and the map freezes
modes.effect: The customer sees a courier who has stopped moving.
modes.cause: The courier drives through a tunnel or a dead zone.
modes.controls: A position older than a minute is dropped, so the map holds still until a fresh one comes in.

modes.mode: Twilio accepts an SMS and the carrier drops it
modes.effect: The customer never gets the confirmation or the courier's arrival message.
modes.cause: The number is wrong, switched off or blocked by the carrier.
modes.controls: None. Plum does not read Twilio's delivery receipts.
modes.action: Read the delivery receipts and alert when fewer than 95% arrive.

modes.effect: Reports run late. Orders carry on.
modes.cause: The cluster is being upgraded, or its disk is full.
modes.controls: Events wait on the stream and are replayed when it is back.
